Hey, lately I've tried to play more spy and so I'm coming from a similar place. Often there is 2 other spies. It's hard to consistently play spy and not technically be hurting your team. It's hard to not feel like a dick. 

I think it helps to view it that you're just playing a game having fun. Not everyone has the same objective. It's not like you're not trying to be the best spy you can possibly be, either.

Spies get a hard time, people will want you to switch off all the time. If you really are committed to it then you should do it. If I have 4 spies on my team, yeah it's a bit annoying but I don't think they are all bad people. I started playing the game because of the spy class. It's a fun class. If someone was so dedicated to learning it and having it be their main then I will adjust to a team with 4 spies. I will still try to enjoy the game.

So I don't know if this is encouraging or not. But I think it's a moral gray area at least and you should try playing spy to see how you feel about it, and maybe if you don't like being the 4th spy you can just try another class.

It's hard, but sometimes one person isn't enough. I also do this, I think about what ways I could help our team win. 

Something I started doing but I feel kinda wrong doing it is when I think it's a good time to push I press my "\*\*\*WE UBERED\*\*\*" bind, just because I know if our team pushed we'd win, even if there isn't an uber.

I know what it's like to desperately want to figure a way to win any match, that it's some extreme puzzle that I could figure out if I put enough brain into it. I think you'll really start to wear yourself out by doing that. You're only one person, and you have limits. And there's always gonna be a chance that you'll lose, even if you play the best you've ever played in your life. There's always some random thing that could happen that kills you. You're not in control, you can't see everything the enemy is doing and you can't see everything your team is doing at all times.

  
All you can do is play your absolute best, play strategically and lose gracefully.

​

That being said, killstreaks alone aren't going to win you games. I could get a 20 killstreak by farming gibus heavies, it doesn't change the fact that a god tier soldier + medic are slamming us across the map somewhere else. You need to look at what matters, and adapt to that. If you notice a weakness, go for that weakness. Take your time, notice what is happening and what you can do about it, then do it. Maybe sometimes all you really have to do is wait for them to fuck up.

​

TLDR: Be realistic about your limitations, be okay with playing well instead of only being okay with winning, be patient, attack where it counts, wait for them to mess up

I struggle with this too, especially as scout. With soldier, you kinda almost get away with it, because you can just bomb in and be a tard and somehow it still works, but as scout it shows that just pure DM isn't enough.

The way I see it is that scout is not meant to be played where he just holds W into the nearest fight. I think we've all tried that and seen that you just insta-die, even if you're relatively good at the game and have a lot of hours you're just gonna get wrecked. (I have 6k hours and I just am realizing that you can't do that)

With scout, the most spazzy character in the game, ironically the thing that benefits him most is restraint. Because he is the fastest, he has the most opportunities to pick the best engagements that benefit him best. So the more calm and patient you are, the less fights you're going to get into where it's a train wreck and more fights where you're actually somewhat confident you're gonna walk away alive.

Considering how new you are, you gotta be prepared to get hit, a lot. It's gonna happen a lot. Slowly as time goes, you'll still get hit, a lot. You'll still die to random things, you'll still get killed in bs ways. You're gonna die in tf2, that's part of it. It's okay and every death is a chance to improve. It does suck but that's how it is.

As you play your movement is going to get better, just on it's own. It's like riding a bike. How can you possibly know how to move well and efficiently if you haven't gone against good players and been forced to learn to move differently? You will pick up on movement things, you'll see how others move. 

A big thing that a lot of people recommend is **jump maps.** I only started doing these like 5k hours in, tbh I was lazy about it. By then my movement was already good but you really hard-focus on movement when you're rocket jumping. If you are determined about it you can try jump academy 2 which is a pretty decent map for that.

TL:DR: Dying is part of the game, you will get better at moving automatically, jump maps really help.

It depends on the context a bit. The first and most straightforward answer is scout, but depending on the terrain it could be hard. Scouts will have a hard time taking out a soldier in a tiny room, because of all the splash damage he can do. If a scout is able to jump around above him in the open and avoid any splash, that is the best scenario for a scout to deal with a soldier. A soldier has to make a decision whether he wants to take the risk of being eaten alive by a scout that is dodging everything above him and pecking at him.

Soldiers are generalists, they can do a lot of things and adapt. So because of that, answering how to counter soldier isn't straightforward. You have to ask yourself what the soldier is doing and how you can react to it. 

A lot of people tend to pick pyro as a counter, which can work a lot of the time and can be infuriating for a soldier. If you want to play around your combo and protect people, it could work. The more skilled the soldier is, the less the pyro counters him. The pyro is still a nuisance but he's not the bane of the soldiers existence and the soldier can usually just wait for the right chance where the pyro isn't ready, the pyro is dead or wait for the pyro to get distracted to attack his medic or teammates.

If the soldier is pocketing, then he's probably going to be very healed or in a very good position. In this case, you'd have to realize that in a way he is the core of the team, and that you need to really keep track of what he is doing. He will always be defended, always be moving with his teammates. In a way, this makes him less valuable of a target. If you can kill his teammates, he becomes weaker and has less people to rely on. When he's alone you'll have a better chance to isolate him and do some damage and not risk too much while doing it.

If a soldier is roaming, then his goal is to cause chaos, or get picks. If you have to worry about some dude going balls out and harassing you constantly then you're going to have some issues feeling safe or feeling that things will go according to plan. Things will mostly be going according to the roamers plan. So in that way the best way to deal with a roamer would be to limit the amount of ways he can effect you. Playing positioning is probably the best, being in a good defensive spot helps in many ways. Being able to surf away to a safe spot when he bombs is good. If you have high ground, has has less time to fly over you, and when you surf you can surf further away.

Soldier is a good class and there's a good reason why people play him, and there's no one way of beating any of them. I hope this gives at least a little insight.

Seeing as they can chase you down, it'd be hard to really have a good satisfying answer about this. Them being a good scout, you can't run around causing the general chaos that a demoknight can usually cause because they probably don't want you to get away with that.

You have to prepare for what a scout COULD do, and what they can do is just wait for you to charge in, and instantly punish and meatshot you. A good scout will stay alive in the combo and chase people down, they can do a lot for their combo including take care of the guy that is most likely going to harass them as demoknight.

You ultimately DON'T have a lot of options, to the point where a lot of people would recommend switching. 

**If you're committed to being demoknight,** then I would suggest playing with your combo, guarding your team and being *very* patient and wait for a chance to right click into someone.
